intro: Hildegard’s antiphon O frondens virga is a monophonic prayer to the Virgin, a single melody without separate accompaniment, in which Mary is greeted as a leafy branch and asked to lift the weak. It is sung here by Makemi.

sections.label: A · Voice greets the Virgin
sections.mNote: A leafy branch, the dawn and an outstretched hand.

cues.title: Syllabic setting with short melismas
cues.text: Makemi sings alone. Most syllables have a single note, and here and there Hildegard sets a vowel to a small group of notes.
cues.evidence: Beverly Lomer describes the setting as primarily syllabic, with neumatic groups and short melismas. The recording source identifies Makemi’s live performance. https://www.hildegard-society.org/2014/10/o-frondens-virga-antiphon.html ; https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:O_frondens_2.ogg

cues.title: Text of the antiphon
cues.text: Hildegard’s twelfth-century prayer opens with Mary standing like a leafy branch in the dawn. In the closing lines the singers ask to be freed from their bad habits and ask her to “stretch out your hand to raise us up”.
cues.evidence: Our translation of Hildegard’s Latin, “atque manum tuam porrige ad erigendum nos”, in the Marian antiphon preserved in the Dendermonde manuscript, fol. 155r. Text and commentary: https://www.hildegard-society.org/2014/10/o-frondens-virga-antiphon.html

cues.title: Mode and range
cues.text: Hildegard built the written melody around D, with A as a second resting place. The line reaches from the A below its home note to the D an octave above it.
cues.evidence: Beverly Lomer identifies D mode, the range A–d′ and the phrase-defining notes D and A in the manuscript. These are the written pitches; the recording’s pitch is unspecified. https://www.hildegard-society.org/2014/10/o-frondens-virga-antiphon.html
cues.how: About the passage as a whole.

fields.label: Work version
fields.value: Monophonic Marian antiphon, performed by a solo singer
fields.note: The Hildegard Society identifies the antiphon in the Dendermonde manuscript, not Ordo virtutum. The recording pages’ dramatic attribution and associated circa-1151 date are rejected. The performer’s edition is unknown.

fields.label: Recorded
